overview: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) is a flagship initiative under the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development, launched to conserve and develop indigenous bovine breeds through genetic upgradation and enhancement of milk production and productivity. It aims to enhance bovine productivity and increase milk production in a sustainable manner using advanced breeding technologies. The mission focuses on the propagation of high genetic merit bulls of indigenous breeds and the establishment of integrated cattle development centres.
objectives: Conservation and development of indigenous bovine breeds
Enhancement of milk production and productivity of bovines
Upgradation of nondescript bovine population using elite indigenous breeds
Distribution of disease-free high genetic merit bulls for natural service
Establishment of integrated indigenous cattle development centres (Gokul Grams)
Promotion of indigenous bovine breeding through professional farm management and superior nutrition
Organization of milk yield competitions and bovine fairs to motivate farmers
Strengthening of bull mother farms to conserve indigenous breeds
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, livestock rearers, dairy cooperatives, self-help groups, gaushalas, NGOs, and state livestock development boards engaged in bovine breeding and development activities. Preference is given to those working with indigenous breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, Rathi, Kankrej, Hariana, Ongole, and others. Beneficiaries must submit a detailed project proposal outlining breed improvement, infrastructure development, and training components.
benefits: Financial assistance for procurement of indigenous bovine breeds, establishment of Gokul Grams, training and capacity building of farmers, organization of infertility camps, fertility camps, and milk yield competitions. Support for semen stations, in-vitro fertilization (IVF) labs, embryo transfer technology, and genomic selection. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, breed improvement advisory, and access to superior germplasm.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid and subsidies for various components such as establishment of Gokul Grams (up to 50% of project cost), procurement of indigenous bovines (up to 50% subsidy), training programs, and infertility/fertility camps. Assistance is released through state implementing agencies based on approved annual action plans and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, breed details, infrastructure plan, budget, and expected outcomes. 2. Submit the proposal to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) or State Livestock Development Board. 3. The SIA forwards the proposal to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) for appraisal. 4. Upon approval by DAHD, funds are released in installments to the SIA. 5. The beneficiary implements the project and submits progress reports and utilization certificates. 6. Final release is made after verification of completion and outcomes.
required_documents: Project proposal with objectives and implementation plan
Details of indigenous bovine breeds to be used
Land documents or lease agreement for project site
Certificate of registration (for NGOs, cooperatives, gaushalas)
Aadhaar and PAN of the beneficiary
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year based on annual action plans of states.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
caveats: Funds are released only after submission of utilization certificates and progress reports
Subsidy is limited to indigenous breeds; exotic or crossbred animals are not eligible for breed procurement support
Projects must be completed within the stipulated timeline as per administrative approval
Beneficiaries must maintain records of bovine progeny and milk yield for monitoring
